--- title: "Cadzow window seams in the CSD" description: "The lfpack Cadzow denoiser left horizontal seams in the CSD at its window boundaries, and a line at each bad channel. Both are fixed in ibl-neuropixel 1.14.0." date: "2026-10-09" date-modified: "2026-10-11" author: "Olivier Winter" categories: [electrophysiology, LFP, CSD, Neuropixels, denoising] --- ## Summary The CSD of Cadzow-denoised LFP (ibl-neuropixel 1.13, as used by lfpack v04) had two artefacts: - **Seams**: horizontal blocks every 32 channels, at the boundaries of Cadzow's spatial windows. - **Bad-channel lines**: one line at each interpolated bad channel. Both are fixed in ibl-neuropixel 1.14.0. The new settings are opt-in, and lfpack v05 uses them. | PR | Change | |---|---| | [ibl-neuropixel#96](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibl-neuropixel/pull/96) | Removes the seams: Cadzow runs on the full probe grid, with Gavish–Donoho shrinkage instead of a hard rank cut. Entry points `cadzow_denoiser_np1` / `cadzow_denoiser_np2`. | | [ibl-neuropixel#97](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibl-neuropixel/pull/97) | Removes the bad-channel lines: Cadzow estimates bad channels instead of interpolating them before and after. | | [lfpack#22](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/lfpack/pull/22) | lfpack picks the NP1 or NP2 settings from the probe geometry. | ## Before and after Each figure shows a 3 s snippet from one of the 11 benchmark insertions. Rows are LFP, bipolar (BPR) and CSD. Columns are no Cadzow, Cadzow before the fix (ibl-neuropixel 1.13) and Cadzow after it (ibl-neuropixel 1.14). The brain regions are on the right. All columns come from the production chunk worker. Each row has one colour scale, so the no-Cadzow CSD saturates. The other 10 insertions are below as thumbnails; click any figure to browse all 11. ![Insertion 749cb2b7: no Cadzow, Cadzow before and after the fix.](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_749cb2b7.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ::: {layout-ncol=4} ![1a276285](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_1a276285.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![1e104bf4](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_1e104bf4.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![6638cfb3](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_6638cfb3.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![d7ec0892](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_d7ec0892.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![da8dfec1](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_da8dfec1.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![dab512bd](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_dab512bd.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![dc7e9403](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_dc7e9403.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![e8f9fba4](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_e8f9fba4.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![eebcaf65](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_eebcaf65.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ![fe380793](figures/2026-10-11_cadzow_before_after_fe380793.webp){.lightbox group="before-after"} ::: In the CSD, the "before" column shows blocks bounded by the window seams (ticks) and lines at the dead channels. The "after" column has neither. It also keeps a little more CSD power (median 0.19 against 0.17 of the no-Cadzow CSD RMS), at the same run time. One artefact is left. In e8f9fba4, a band remains at channels 170–195: the neighbours of the labelled noisy channels are noisy too (2–3.6× the noise level), but they are not labelled. That is a channel-labelling issue, not a Cadzow one. ## Why there were seams Cadzow fits a low-rank model in windows of 64 channels, blended every 32 channels. The CSD is a second spatial derivative, so any disagreement between two neighbouring window fits shows up as a seam. The fits disagreed for two reasons: 1. **NP1 checkerboard.** Each NP1 row holds only 2 of the 4 lateral positions. Half of Cadzow's trajectory matrix was zeros, and the SVD treated them as data. The fix fills the empty positions from their neighbours. 2. **Hard adaptive rank.** Neighbouring windows kept different numbers of components. The fix shrinks the singular values smoothly (Gavish–Donoho) instead of cutting them. Bad channels were interpolated before and after Cadzow. An interpolated channel does not follow the local curvature that the CSD measures, so it leaves a line. The fix treats bad channels like the empty grid positions, so that Cadzow estimates them. ## Validation on a synthetic field The synthetic field has 40 laminar current sources forward-modelled onto NP1, with 3 % white noise. Its true CSD is known. The bad channels are those of e8f9fba4 (11 dead, 7 noisy). ::: {#tbl-synthetic .cell tbl-cap='Synthetic field, 3 % noise. CSD error: median per-channel RMS error against the true CSD, relative to the true CSD RMS, near bad channels and elsewhere. Seam ratio: error within ±2 channels of a window boundary over the error elsewhere; 1 means no seams.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
CSD error CSD error near bad channels seam ratio
ibl-neuropixel 1.13 0.81 0.95 2.08
#96: full grid + shrinkage 0.31 0.58 1.09
#96 + #97: bad channels estimated 0.31 0.30 1.21
``` ::: ::: Without bad channels, the CSD error is 0.29, the same as with #97. The PR figures show the synthetic field. ::: {layout-ncol=2} ![#96: true CSD, ibl-neuropixel 1.13 and full grid + shrinkage, without noise (top) and at 3 % noise (bottom).](figures/2026-10-10_cadzow_pr96_fill_grid_shrinkage.webp){#fig-pr96 .lightbox} ![#97: bad channels interpolated against estimated by Cadzow (triangles: dead in black, noisy in red).](figures/2026-10-10_cadzow_pr97_bad_channels.webp){#fig-pr97 .lightbox} ::: ## Compatibility - With its defaults, `cadzow_denoiser` gives the same output as in 1.13.0, bit for bit. - The shrinkage scale was calibrated on white noise: 2.25 for NP1 and 1.22 for NP2. The NP1 value brings the seams back on NP2, hence the two entry points. - Multi-shank probes are not supported yet by the full-grid option. - In lfpack v05, file sizes per tier do not change. Fidelity to the denoised input is about 2 dB lower, and the codec, not Cadzow, now limits the CSD. See [lfpack v05](../2026-10-lfpack-v05/index.qmd). ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Code, data and earlier attempts | File | Content | |---|---| | `plot_before_after.py` | Before / after figures on this page | | `cadzow_synthetic*.py`, `cadzow_fill.py`, `cadzow_shrink*.py` | Synthetic field, full-grid fill, shrinkage prototypes | | `cadzow_bad_real.py`, `cadzow_synthetic_bad.py` | Bad channels as missing grid positions | | `cadzow_pr_figures.py` | PR figures, with the ibldsp API | The cached chunks are in `~/scratch/lfp/csd_lfpack_v04/`, made by `../2026-10-csd/plot_cadzow_csd.py`. Before the synthetic field, three remedies changed the blending of the windows: staggered runs (`cadzow_stagger.py`), cycle spinning (`cadzow_cycle_spin.py`) and more overlap (`ovx = 48`). None of them removed the seams, because the fits themselves disagreed. MSSA (`cadzow_mssa_real.py`) denoised too little. :::
